decisions.note: Maker's round-1 spec had duplicate-save just notify 'already saved'; client supplied the reference-correct behavior of jumping straight to editing the existing bookmark.
Round-1 spec's search covered only title/address/tags and wasn't case-insensitive; client asked for note-text inclusion and case-insensitivity, both never surfaced by maker.
Round-1 spec only auto-captured the title; client asked for favicon and description auto-capture, which the maker had not proposed.
Round-1 spec offered only newest-first ordering; client requested alphabetical-by-title sort, a reference item never surfaced.
Round-1 spec had no tag autocomplete; client asked for existing-tag suggestions on entry, matching REF-BM-10, which the maker had not offered.
Maker explicitly scoped import out of v1; client rejected that exclusion and required it be kept in scope.
Round-2 import spec (FR-016/017) didn't preserve browser-folder structure; client asked that folders become tags, a reference-required behavior (preserving tags) not surfaced.
Round-2 import spec didn't preserve original save dates; client required original dates be kept so newest-sort stays meaningful, matching the reference's 'date added' preservation rule.
Maker had parked/deferred export entirely; client rejected the deferral and required at least basic export be kept in scope, citing anti-lock-in concerns.
Notes were plain text in the spec as presented; client asked for markdown-style formatting (bold/links/bullets) rendered on read-back, matching REF-BM-23, not previously surfaced.

Implementation folded the distinct 'description' entity field into the free-form note field rather than keeping it separate/editable in its own right; client explicitly affirmed this as 'exactly what I'd hoped,' a satisficing miss against the entity model.

Round-7 build presented tag filter and text search as separate/exclusive mechanisms; client asked to combine a tag with a search term (tag+text AND), the edge-case rule in the reference, which the presentation hadn't surfaced as working.
Round-7 search had no exact-phrase matching; client explicitly requested quoted-phrase exact match (REF-BM-16), a real gap the maker confirmed and tracked, later implemented in round 10.
